body:
> So in the end, the usecase being "hide hits when no query" and not "do not do any search when query is empty", we could mark this as fixed and answer the person..

Yes but since you qualified it as bug, I don't know :) For now, if it's an acceptable workaround (change the UI behaviour, not the InstantSearch.js behaviour), go for it.

However since I've checked [the InstantSearch.js code](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/2ed948dcae94f0b6ca217a083acc8ad2e6337754/src/lib/url-sync.js#L136-L140), I have the feeling we might be able to do something. What happens is that we setup the mechanics to bind the search to the browser URL during the first rendering. The idea is that this way we prevent the first rendering to update the URL. The thing we want to avoid is an update to an empty query URL which will have at least `?q=`, which is weird because happened yet.

But there might be a way to fix that. The code [retrieves the state from the URL before the start](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/lib/url-sync.js#L117-L120) of InstantSearch.js lifecycle. This means that during the first rendering, we are able to figure out if the current state of the search is different from the initial parameters. If it's different then we should update the URL, otherwise we keep the same.

What do you think @vvo ?
